sources.title: Simo Särkkä, Bayesian Filtering and Smoothing (2013)
sources.locator: Author-hosted 252-page PDF; the complete relevant proof units were inspected. Chapter 8 §8.1, Theorem 8.1 and equations (8.2)–(8.4), printed pp. 134–135 (PDF pp. 153–154): fixed-interval backward factorization and Markov conditional identity. §8.2, Theorem 8.2 and equations (8.5)–(8.15), printed pp. 135–137 (PDF pp. 154–156): RTS recursion and its Gaussian conditioning derivation.

contents.name: Chapter 8 §8.1, Theorem 8.1, equations (8.2)–(8.4): backward smoothing identity and conditional independence given the next state
contents.reason: Defines the all-observation marginal target; the source's density factorization is treated as the classical formulation, while the local definition states the data-indexed RCD version and its version freedom.

contents.name: Chapter 8 §8.2, Theorem 8.2, equations (8.7)–(8.11): one-step joint Gaussian and backward conditional law
contents.reason: Supports the backward Gaussian parameters. The local proof derives the future-observation kernel factorization without densities, applies the exact positive-definite observed-block conditioner, and states the forecast-covariance boundary.

contents.name: Chapter 8 §8.2, Theorem 8.2, equations (8.5)–(8.15): terminal initialization, backward mean/covariance recursion, and derivation by Gaussian conditioning
contents.reason: Supports the classical procedure. The local algorithm makes the inverse domain explicit and uses an SPD Cholesky solve; it makes no stability claim.

contents.name: Chapter 8 §§8.1–8.2, Theorems 8.1–8.2 and complete derivation through equation (8.15)
contents.reason: The source supplies the standard RTS derivation in its density-based Gaussian setting. The local proof supplies the complete kernel/RCD argument, the Gaussian-mixture step, PSD covariance conclusion, and exact forecast-covariance boundary.

contents.name: Chapter 8 §8.2, equation (8.6): the RTS gain uses the inverse one-step forecast covariance
contents.reason: The source's gain formula displays the ordinary forecast inverse. The local example verifies a singular-forecast boundary directly and does not attribute a pseudoinverse extension to the source.

sources.title: Kody Law, Andrew M. Stuart, and Konstantinos Zygalakis, Data Assimilation: A Mathematical Introduction (2015)
sources.locator: Complete author manuscript PDF inspected at the full relevant proof unit. Chapter 3 §3.1, Theorem 3.1 and its proof, printed pp. 54–55 (PDF pp. 54–56): the linear-Gaussian full-path smoothing law, block-tridiagonal precision, quadratic-form derivation, and positive-definiteness argument under C₀, Σ, Γ ≻ 0.

contents.name: Chapter 3 §3.1, Theorem 3.1 and complete proof: Gaussian smoothing law characterized by a block-tridiagonal precision matrix
contents.reason: An independent full-text treatment confirms Gaussianity of the smoothed path and the positive-definite covariance regime. It does not supply the RTS backward recursion or the singular-PSD cases; neither is attributed to it.

contents.name: Chapter 3 §3.1, linear-Gaussian stochastic-dynamics and observation model preceding Theorem 3.1
contents.reason: Supports the fixed-interval all-data smoothing interpretation in the full-rank density setting; the local definition keeps the RCD version convention explicit.

contents.name: Chapter 3 §3.1, Theorem 3.1 proof: density quadratic form, Hessian precision, and strict positivity from positive-definite initial and process covariances
contents.reason: The source proof is a batch quadratic-form route, not the local one-step backward conditional-kernel argument; its positive-definite density assumptions do not justify the lemma's PSD state-covariance scope.

contents.name: Chapter 3 §3.1, Theorem 3.1: positive-definite Gaussian full-path smoothing model
contents.reason: The source assumes positive-definite initial and noise covariance matrices, so it does not cover this degenerate boundary example; the local RCD identity is verified directly.

item_arguments.argument: Define the marginal, data-indexed RCD target of X_k given the complete finite observation history. State explicitly that the definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness on null histories; the theorem constructs a Gaussian version.

Extend the exact filtering kernel by the independent process noise and push it through X_{k+1}=F_{k+1}X_k+q_{k+1}. The independent Gaussian stack is jointly Gaussian; apply the BCS-03 conditional-law theorem with observed block P_{k+1|k} ≻ 0 to obtain C_k and a PSD Schur complement. Then factor the finite-horizon path law into past, transition, and future kernels and verify by iterated kernel integration that future observations do not change this backward conditional kernel.

Give the exact terminal initialization and descending backward pass using the one-step forecast covariance. Require every forecast matrix inverted by the recursion to be SPD and specify a Cholesky triangular solve; make no complexity or numerical-stability claim.

Start with the exact terminal filtering kernel and induct backward. Compose the backward RCD with the next smoothed kernel, verify the conditional event identity, and realize the Gaussian affine-kernel mixture on a finite product probability space. The independent Gaussian stack lemma identifies the affine image as Gaussian; the resulting covariance is the stated RTS update and remains PSD.

For a scalar two-transition random walk, compute all forward innovations, gains and covariances, then both backward gains and smoothed moments exactly. Apply the local theorem to identify the resulting Gaussian law as the fixed-interval conditional version.

Use a deterministic zero state with a positive observation-noise variance. The forward innovation is SPD and filtering is defined, but the state forecast covariance is zero, so the ordinary RTS inverse is undefined. Verify directly that the smoothing law is the point mass at zero and assert no pseudoinverse extension.
